payload.task: Self-diffusion coefficient of Cu in a perfect fcc Cu crystal at 300 K by molecular dynamics
payload.reason: Premise check fails: the quantity is not measurable with MD for this system and condition. (1) In a perfect (defect-free) fcc crystal there is no diffusion mechanism at all: lattice self-diffusion in Cu is vacancy-mediated, and a perfect periodic cell holds no vacancies. Spontaneous Frenkel-pair formation costs several eV and never happens at 300 K (exp(-E/kT) with kT = 0.026 eV). (2) Even in a real crystal at thermal-equilibrium vacancy concentration, Arrhenius extrapolation of high-temperature tracer data (activation energy about 2 eV) gives D(300 K) of order 1e-36 cm2/s (roughly 1e-37 to 1e-35 depending on the D0/Q set used). The equilibrium vacancy site fraction at 300 K is about exp(-1.2 to -1.3 eV/kT), roughly 1e-21, so an MD cell of 1e3 to 1e6 atoms contains no vacancy. (3) Resolution: with ns-scale MD the smallest resolvable D is about (0.01 A^2)/(6 x 1 ns), roughly 2e-10 cm2/s, which is more than 25 orders of magnitude above the physical value. The MSD of a 300 K perfect crystal just plateaus at the thermal-vibration value <u^2> (about 0.02 to 0.03 A^2 for 3 coordinates, Debye-Waller), so a fitted slope would be fitting noise, drift, or integrator or thermostat artifacts. Reporting such a number as D would be wrong. The physically correct statement is: D_MD = 0 within resolution (an upper bound of about 1e-10 cm2/s), while the true value is about 1e-36 cm2/s, set by thermally activated vacancies that MD cannot sample. Well-posed alternatives, which I can run if requested: (a) vacancy-mediated D(T) for Cu: get the vacancy formation and migration energies with the MLIP (relaxations + NEB) and combine them with the fcc correlation factor f = 0.781 in D = f a^2 c_v Gamma, then extrapolate to 300 K with an explicit Arrhenius uncertainty. Validate against measured tracer D at 1000 to 1350 K. (b) Direct MD diffusion where it is measurable: liquid Cu above Tm (1358 K), validating the potential's melting point against the tier1 calibration value, or a cell with a fixed injected vacancy at high T (D_vacancy, rescaled by c_v). (c) Report the 300 K vibrational MSD / Debye-Waller factor, which MD can measure. No MD was run, because no simulation of the stated setup could produce a meaningful value.
